question: What does Illinois SB 315 require of third-party auditors of large frontier developers, and from when?

scope.included: Law-firm client alerts on SB 315 published July 2026 (Crowell & Moring, Latham & Watkins, Davis Wright Tremaine); the Akerman note on the signing date.
scope.excluded: The statutory text itself; enforcement practice; other states' laws.
scope.comparison_target: Summaries that say 'Illinois requires AI audits' compared with the threshold, the independence test and the start date in the alerts.

sources.title: Illinois AI Safety Measures Act SB 315: What Frontier AI Developers Must Do Before January 2028

exact_spans.quote: beginning January 1, 2028, large frontier developers to undergo annual audits by independent third parties
neither the auditor nor the large frontier developer may have a financial interest in the other party
On July 6, 2026, Illinois Governor JB Pritzker signed SB 315

sources.title: Illinois Joins Growing State-Level Effort to Regulate Frontier AI With New Safety Measures Act

exact_spans.quote: frontier model developers that earned more than $500 million in revenue in the preceding year must retain an independent third party
On July 7, 2026, Illinois Governor JB Pritzker signed Senate Bill 315

sources.title: Illinois Enacts Frontier AI Safety Law

exact_spans.quote: the large frontier AI framework and audit obligations begin January 1, 2028

results.proposition: Under Illinois SB 315 as summarized by three law firms, large frontier developers (revenue above $500 million in the preceding year) must undergo annual audits by independent third parties beginning January 1, 2028, and neither auditor nor developer may hold a financial interest in the other.
results.interpretation: The independence test is the financial-interest rule from financial audit; the obligation is annual and starts in 2028 for the largest developers only.
results.warrant: Each element appears in at least one alert; the start date appears in two.

scope.dataset_or_population: SB 315 as summarized by Crowell, Latham and DWT
scope.metric_scope: Statutory requirements as summarized; not the text

claim_atoms.text: The statutory text has not been read directly.

results.uncertainty: Secondary summaries by counsel; wording of the statute may differ.

results.proposition: Two alerts give different signing dates for SB 315: July 6, 2026 (Crowell) and July 7, 2026 (Latham).
results.interpretation: A one-day discrepancy in secondary sources; the bill record would settle it.
results.warrant: Both dates are quoted from the alerts.
